instruction.name: movscr2gr
instruction.description: Copy the value in the scratch register selected by scrj (0-3) to rd.

throughput.name: 8 independent lanes
throughput.asm: movscr2gr $r12, $scr0; movscr2gr $r13, $scr0; movscr2gr $r14, $scr0; movscr2gr $r15, $scr0; movscr2gr $r16, $scr0; movscr2gr $r17, $scr0; movscr2gr $r18, $scr0; movscr2gr $r19, $scr0
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 100 --unroll2 200 --iters 2000 --warmup 10 --reps 9 --core 0 --init 'movgr2scr $scr0, $r0; movgr2scr $scr1, $r0; movgr2scr $scr2, $r0; movgr2scr $scr3, $r0' --asm 'movscr2gr $r12, $scr0; movscr2gr $r13, $scr0; movscr2gr $r14, $scr0; movscr2gr $r15, $scr0; movscr2gr $r16, $scr0; movscr2gr $r17, $scr0; movscr2gr $r18, $scr0; movscr2gr $r19, $scr0'
throughput.notes: 8 independent movscr2gr instructions reading scr0 retire in 4.00 cycles, i.e. 2 per cycle (CPI 0.5). The body must be kept small: with --unroll 5000 (8 x 5000 = 40k instructions, 160 KiB) the sequence no longer fits in L1I and the measured CPI rises to about 1.0, which is a fetch limit rather than the instruction throughput. Measured on 2026-11-17 on LA464, core 0.

notes: LBT scratch-register move. movgr2scr + movscr2gr round trip is 4.01 cycles and only the sum is observable, so no per-direction latency is recorded. Throughput is 2 per cycle (CPI 0.5) with an L1I-resident body.
